# Teacher reference and original rubric
Separate, not access-protected. The original 40-mark rubric allocates 6 to investigation/requirements; 8 to design/schema/dictionary; 10 to implementation/reports/controlled changes; 10 to testing/import/transactions/recovery; and 6 to demonstration/authorship/evaluation. It is a draft, not official weighting; school conditions govern any assessment adaptation. Use the explanations as practice feedback and accept equivalent valid designs.

The default reference uses SQLite in memory, explicit transactions and enabled foreign keys. Booking rejects full-session S01 requests, duplicates, unknown IDs and date errors without changing the data. M03/S02 succeeds once, then the repeated pair is rejected. Attendance can be updated only for a booked pair; Boolean objects and values outside 0 or 1 are rejected. Import validates M-plus-two-digit IDs and names, then inserts atomically. Existing IDs raise IntegrityError and roll back the batch. The raw CSV's blank name causes rejection; the cleaned CSV supplies three valid imports.

Schema constraints remain as described earlier. Direct SQL can bypass application capacity and date rules. The reference has no trigger, GUI, login, ODBC driver or persistent-storage workflow. SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE serialises the writer's check-and-insert operation; busy failures propagate rather than being retried. The reference expects no active caller transaction.

The recovery demonstration uses the backup API to copy into another in-memory database and verifies integrity, references and content. A saved, reopened restore needs separate evidence. Operational retention, history and security remain unresolved. Review each R1–R7 requirement with expected and actual results, rather than screenshots alone.
